newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Double-digit growth seen for Singapore disk drives.
newsitem.headline: Double-digit growth seen for Singapore disk drives.

text.p: Singapore expects double-digit growth in its hard disk drive output in 1996, despite the recent slowdown in the electronics industry, Economic Development Board Chairman Philip Yeo said on Wednesday.
Speaking at the opening of a new plant, Yeo said:
"Barring unforeseen negative developments, we should be able to achieve double-digit growth in 1996 in this sector, both in unit and sales over 1995."

Yeo said some 24 million hard disk drives valued at Singapore $7.8 billion were produced in the first-half of 1996, representing increases of about 30 percent and 40 percent respectively over the same period of 1995.
Production of high-end disk drive manufacturing in Singapore was expanding, Yeo said.
In 1995, 27 percent of the island republic's hard disk drive output had capacity of one gigabyte and above, he said.
"We expect the ratio of such disk drives manufactured in Singapore to increase to over 60 percent for 1996," he said.
